item.title: Qatar Works to Bridge Gap in US Iran Talks
item.description:
Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al-Ansari says mediators are shuttling between capitals and exchanging proposals in an effort to restart negotiations between the US and Iran, with teams working around the clock to bridge remaining differences. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Al-Ansari says Qatar’s priorities are ending the conflict and restoring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, warning that restrictions on international waterways could set a dangerous precedent.
At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Marsh CEO Says Geopolitics Tops CEO Risks
item.description:
Marsh CEO & President John Doyle says geopolitical tensions and their impact on trade and supply chains are among the biggest concerns facing corporate leaders, while emerging technology is adding to cyber threats. Doyle also tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that AI offers significant opportunities for growth and productivity but warns that systemic cyber risk stemming from new technologies remains poorly understood.
At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI’s Wobbly House of Cards Puts Markets and US Economy at Risk
item.description: The heads of America’s leading AI development labs have started a national conversation about tapping the brakes on a technology that’s offering so much promise for society, while at the same time showing it can do a frightening amount of harm.
item.dc:creator: Jeran Wittenstein

item.title: Qatar Airways Bets on Fleet and Cargo Growth
item.description: Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Qatar Airways Group CEO Hamad Ali Al-Khater says passenger demand remains resilient despite regional conflict and sharply higher jet fuel costs, with travelers booking closer to departure and the carrier shifting capacity toward its most profitable routes. The airline plans to take delivery of 138 aircraft over the next five years while expanding its cargo business and continuing its Starlink rollout. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Global Conflicts Shape High Stakes UN Meetings
item.description:
World leaders are gathering in New York for the UN General Assembly as escalating Middle East tensions, the war in Ukraine and pressure on global energy supplies dominate the diplomatic agenda. Bloomberg News managing editor for European economy & government Ben Sills and CNN senior national security reporter Jennifer Hansler join Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss Europe’s push for Ukrainian air defenses, the US approach to the Houthis and the prospects for diplomacy as Saudi Arabia faces renewed attacks.
At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EM Investors Are Favoring Local Bonds as Dollar Debt Lags
item.description: Emerging-market investors are for now sticking with local-currency sovereign debt as surging Treasury yields dim the appeal of dollar-denominated developing-nation bonds.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Wong

item.title: Volvo Car Picks Škoda Boss Zellmer as New CEO to Oversee Revamp
item.description: Volvo Car AB’s board of directors appointed Klaus Zellmer as president and chief executive officer to replace Håkan Samuelsson, who’s set to step down next year.
item.dc:creator: Albertina Torsoli

item.title: Inside Jefferies’ Months-Long Tussle With Glencore Over Radiant
item.description: Executives at Jefferies Financial Group Inc. were sounding increasingly irate.
item.dc:creator: Jack Farchy and Alfred Cang

item.title: China Names Li Chenggang Its Top International Trade Negotiator
item.description: China on Sunday elevated the title of a key member of its team handling talks with the US, hours before delegations from the two countries were set to hold negotiations in New York.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Cracks in Europe’s Junk Property Debt Revive Fears of 2023 Pain
item.description: European real estate debt is starting to show the strain of higher interest rates, with a slump in riskier bonds and the rare cancellation of a new junk issue.
item.dc:creator: Libby Cherry and Eleanor Duncan

item.title: Tata’s Rival Camps Lawyer Up Ahead of Looming Legal Battle
item.description: The parties fighting for control over India’s Tata Group have retained some of the country’s most prominent law firms and advocates, as they dig in for a protracted and high-profile battle.
item.dc:creator: Menaka Doshi

item.title: Yen Is Vulnerable With Japan on Holiday After BOJ Disappoints
item.description: The yen is vulnerable to sharp moves and further declines over the next week, with a three-day holiday in Japan set to reduce trading liquidity and investors disappointed that the central bank didn’t offer stronger guidance on the pace of future interest rate hikes.
item.dc:creator: Hideyuki Sano and Umesh Desai

item.title: Hong Kong’s Chan Says City to Expand Market for Dim Sum Bonds
item.description: Hong Kong plans to expand the Dim Sum bond market and develop the yuan-denominated gold and commodity markets to further enhance the city’s financial role and pricing power, Financial Secretary Paul Chan wrote in his weekly blog Sunday.
item.dc:creator: K. Oanh Ha

item.title: Heavy Rain Disrupts Trains in Japan as Tropical Storm Approaches
item.description: The approaching tropical cyclone Dujuan could cause suspensions and delays on train lines in the greater Tokyo area, with possible disruptions from as early as Sunday evening through Tuesday morning, major operator East Japan Railway Co. warned.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Maekawa

item.title: Australia Home Auction Clearance Rates Fall Amid Rate Hike Fears
item.description: Australia’s residential real estate market remained subdued with auction clearance rates falling this week as concerns the central bank will increase interest rates later this month grow, according to property researcher Cotality.
item.dc:creator: Edward Johnson

item.title: Venezuela, TotalEnergies Pave Way for Oil Company’s Return
item.description: Venezuela and TotalEnergies SE signed a memorandum of understanding on Saturday, setting up the French company for a return to operations in the South American country.
item.dc:creator: Jose Orozco and Fabiola Zerpa

item.title: Trump Reignites Kennedy Center Fight
item.description: President Donald Trump’s plans for the Kennedy Center are hitting legal roadblocks as questions mount over the landmark’s future. Bloomberg’s Shaquille Omari breaks down the escalating battle over one of Washington’s most iconic cultural institutions. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hormuz Oil Shipments Hit Six-Month High, US Commander Says
item.description: Oil and liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz in the past two weeks reached the highest level in six months, signaling that US naval protection and mine clearance efforts are “paying off,” a regional US commander said.
item.dc:creator: Tony Czuczka

item.title: Companies Avoid Selling the Bonds Investors Crave: Credit Weekly
item.description: Investors are clamoring for the kind of debt companies are reluctant to sell now: longer-term bonds.
item.dc:creator: Emily Graffeo, Caleb Mutua, Finbarr Flynn and Ronan Martin

item.title: Can India Turn Its Promise Into Prosperity?
item.description: Blackstone COO Jon Gray says India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are drawing interest from global investors. But India’s demographic advantage also creates pressure: millions of young people graduate every year, while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. At the same time, Indian states are competing aggressively for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors. The question is whether India can turn its scale, talent and investment momentum into enough productive jobs to sustain its growth. (Source: Bloomberg)
